Worker05's source-bound review at frozen base `e000d66dd26ab053e9b17ce7bf8d3c873c3dde99` found `data/ingredients/mapped/Sea_Salts.yaml` still uses `NCIT:C75874` as its primary identity even though its own history describes only contextual evidence for a supplier-qualified commercial sea-salts preparation.

The captured [NCIT:C75874 term](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/api/ontologies/ncit/terms?iri=http%3A%2F%2Fpurl.obolibrary.org%2Fobo%2FNCIT_C75874) supplies a “Sea Salt” label but does not substantiate equivalence to the source product. [Sigma S9883](https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/US/en/product/sigma/s9883) illustrates why catalog-specific review matters: the supplier page contains both generic sea-salt prose and an artificial-seawater mixture description. It does not identify every generic Sea Salt occurrence or establish that this owner is catalog S9883. The review does not assert an unverified natural-versus-artificial NCIT definition.

The independently revised proposal uses a local registry identity and FALLBACK_REGISTRY mapping, withdraws the unsupported exact/close NCIT relationship, and preserves its historical provenance. It does not infer a catalog number, formula, component list, or merge with Artificial_Sea_Salt. All existing holds remain. The first draft's retained closeMatch was rejected during skeptical review and corrected before handoff.

Before-owner SHA256: `7d10257ca3847166f949d8e179aa068c6ebef128f932769b29ca064b76595c39`. Exact source cases, primary captures, proposal bytes and independent review are in `reports/all_unmatched_20261107/worker-05/materials/` and `chemicals/materials-independent-review.*` on `review/all-unmatched-w05-source-review-20261107`.

Follow-up: reconcile shared-owner proposals and source-specific product boundaries, apply through guarded writers, withdraw inherited changed-payload support, and regenerate synchronized surfaces only during coordinator integration. Native release admission remains required (#1165). #811 records a missing generic Sea Salt index answer and #312 discussed Artificial_Sea_Salt; neither establishes this supplier owner's identity. Live issue/body/comment deduplication receipts are in the worker bundle. This review made no maintained-data or downstream-build changes.
title: Sea_Salts retains an unsupported NCIT primary identity for a supplier-scoped preparation

body:
Found in adversarial review of #505.

All 107 records created by `create_records_from_groundings.py` have no
`ingredient_type`. The field is not schema-required, so nothing failed -- but it is
what `WHOLE_MEDIUM_TYPES` and the NAMED_MEDIUM / UNDEFINED_MIXTURE /
SINGLE_INGREDIENT routing key off, and several of the new records are plainly not
single ingredients:

```
MICRO:0001715  Artificial seawater
MICRO:0000520  Clarified rumen fluid
MICRO:0000521  Sludge fluid
MICRO:0001598  Hemin solution
MICRO:0000456  trace metals 44
MICRO:0000567  Heart Infusion Agar
```

`classify_ingredient_type.py` lives in culturebotai-claw and is the writer for this
field, so filling it is a cross-repo run rather than something #505 should do inline
-- and claw is the repo that would otherwise overwrite whatever MIM wrote (the #148
pattern).

Until it runs, any consumer that filters on `ingredient_type` silently excludes these
107 records. `cross_reference_culturemech.py` is one such consumer: its
`WHOLE_MEDIUM_TYPES` filter is how #490 came to return a confident 0 candidates.
title: The 107 records created from the CultureMech residual have no ingredient_type

Worker04 found four source defects that need upstream reconciliation before source-specific matching can be released. This MIM tracking issue records the integration blockers; it does not authorize changing CultureMech from this worker.

All four current CultureMech `main` files were read through GitHub on 2026-11-08 at 05:13–05:21 UTC and matched the frozen case bytes. Captures, hashes and primary references are retained in `reports/all_unmatched_20261107/worker-04/captures/current-issue-owners/` on branch `review/all-unmatched-w04-source-review-20261107`.

| Source record | Observed conflict | Required follow-up |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data/normalized_yaml/algae/merds_my75s.yaml` | Ingredient `Thoroughly disperse the agar in cold`, with75%w/v, is a preparation-sentence fragment. The [CCAP MErds/MY75S sheet](https://www.ccap.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/MR_MErds_MY75S.pdf) describes a biphasic medium with separate recipes and stock bases. The normalized two-ingredient record is not a faithful reconstruction. | Remove the phantom token while reconstructing the entire phase/stock structure and preparation instructions from the source; do not treat75% seawater as75% agar or just delete one row. |
| `data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/isosphaera_medium.yaml` | `Agar, Noble (BD214050), if needed` combines Noble grade with a catalog number that [BD identifies as Bacto Agar](https://www.bdbiosciences.com/en-ca/products/reagents/dehydrated-culture-media/agars/agar-bottle-100g.214050?tab=product_details). [Noble Agar214220](https://www.bd.com/en-us/products-and-solutions/products/product-page.214220) is a different product. | Recover the original ATCC recipe/version or procurement evidence and decide which field was wrong. Retain the contradictory raw label until resolved. |
| `data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/JCM_J1429_M1H_NAG_ASW.yaml` | Free N-acetyl-D-glucosamine is annotated CHEBI:8006 (peptidoglycan context), while [JCM1429](https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=1429) lists the free ingredient, consistent with CHEBI:506227. | Correct the upstream monomer grounding with primary recipe and ontology evidence. The MIM spelling proposal must not conceal this upstream error. |
| `data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/aam.yaml` | The record calls its source AAM-minus but includes D-glutamate1.71mM. [Lee2009](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2698402/) Table4 row13 gives L-glutamic acid250mg for AAM; the Methods explicitly omit L-glutamic acid from AAM-minus. | Reconstruct the intended AAM/AAM-minus variant and stereochemistry, rather than changing D to L alone. Do not extend this correction to the separate Klein1979 occurrences without their original methods. |

Related, but different, work: CultureMech#408 concerns TOGO volume-to-g/L normalization; the closed CultureMech#273 parsing correction concerned SBBM, not this CCAP MErds/MY75S record. MIM#587 concerns KG instructional labels; its comments retract blanket parenthetical filtering. These four findings need source-specific fixes, not generic label stripping.

Acceptance: each corrected source cites its original evidence, preserves recipe variants and supplied forms, gets independent source review, and is then reconciled with frozen MIM case IDs and holds during the coordinator's integration. No maintained file or export has been changed by worker04. Campaign dependency #1158 and publication holds #1157 remain active.

Deduplication searched the complete retrieved MIM and CultureMech issue/PR title/body inventories plus relevant prior comments. No exact open task for these four records was found within that bounded search; this is not a claim that every historical comment was searched.
title: Track four primary-source conflicts blocking worker04 source-specific matches

body:
Surfaced independently by **all three** Edison/PaperQA3 literature runs during the #148 validation (2026-08-02), each unprompted, each phrasing it as a warning:

- **Blood Agar Base** — "`DEFINED_MEDIUM` should be understood as the project's named-medium record type, **not a claim that every molecular constituent and concentration is chemically specified**."
- **Soil+Seawater Medium** — "may be retained if it means 'complete named medium,' but **it must not be interpreted as 'chemically defined medium'**."
- **Leptospira Medium Base EMJH** — "'defined' **should not be interpreted as chemically defined**."

## Why this matters

In microbiology, "defined medium" is a term of art meaning *chemically* defined — every constituent known and quantified. That is the **opposite** of what these records contain: complex digests, infusions, and extracts (blood agar base, heart infusion broth, soil+seawater).

MIM's enum means "complete named medium formulation". The schema *description* supports that reading:

> Complete medium formulation or recipe with multiple ingredients (e.g., R2A agar, LB broth, Marine agar 2216, Oatmeal agar). Should cross-reference to CultureMech for full recipe.

but the enum **name** actively contradicts it. The pair is what makes it misleading: `UNDEFINED_MIXTURE`, sitting in the same enum, *does* carry the compositional meaning ("unknown or variable composition"), so a reader reasonably infers `DEFINED_MEDIUM` is its compositional opposite.

**53 records now carry this value** (as of #167) and kg-microbe consumes it.

## Options

1. **Description-only (low risk, recommended first).** Sharpen the `DEFINED_MEDIUM` description in `src/mediaingredientmech/schema/mediaingredientmech.yaml` to state explicitly that it denotes record granularity — a complete *named* medium — not chemical definedness, and that complex undefined components are expected and normal.
2. **Rename (honest but cross-repo).** CultureMech imports MIM's enums, so a rename needs coordination and a migration. Weigh against option 1.

Evidence: three Edison reports under `research/ingredients/` (gitignored) — `Blood_Agar_Base-`, `Soilseawater_Medium-`, `Leptospira_Medium_Base_EMJH-edison-literature.md`.
title: DEFINED_MEDIUM reads as "chemically defined" — enum name contradicts its own description

body:
Follow-up to #218 / #224. #224 built the detection and triage; this is the execution.

`mappings/duplicate_identifier_baseline.tsv` now marks **15 groups `SAFE_MERGE`** — verified by reading the records, not inferred:

- pure spelling variants — `Glycerol`/`glycerol`, `Glycyl-glycine`/`Glycylglycine`, `Sea water`/`Seawater`, the two poly(L-lysine) spellings
- redundant stereo descriptors — `D-Sucrose`/`Sucrose`, `Glutathione`/`L-Glutathione`
- `X` vs `X (role annotation)` from the communitymech import — `Acetate (carbon source)`, `Ammonium chloride (nitrogen source)`, `Sodium nitrate (nitrogen source)`, `Sodium metasilicate (silicate for diatom frustules)`
- salt-name variants — `Ampicillin sodium salt`/`Na-ampicillin`, `Calcium D-Pantothenate`/`Calcium pantothenate`
- `Bacto X` vs `Bacto X (Difco)` — MICRO:0000113, MICRO:0000114
- CHEBI:16991 `Deoxyribonucleic acid from herring sperm`/`Fish-Sperm DNA` — one reagent

Precedent exists: CHEBI:63005 already carries a synonym sourced `merged_from_duplicate_mim_record`.

## Why this needs new tooling

No current script implements record-merge semantics. `promote_resolved_unmapped.py` promotes; `apply_microbedecoder_residual_merges.py` (#214) folds an **UNMAPPED** record into a mapped one, which is a different case — both records here are MAPPED and each may carry:

1. **occurrence_statistics** — `Glycerol` has 208/54, `glycerol` has 6/6. Summing `total_occurrences` is right; summing `media_count` over-counts if a medium lists both spellings. Needs a decision.
2. **role facets** — both `Glycerol` records carry roles; `Glycyl-glycine` has roles and `Glycylglycine` does not. Union, or keep the survivor's?
3. **SSSOM rows** — subjects are keyed on `preferred_term` of MAPPED records, so deleting the loser **orphans its row**. Both `MIM:Glycyl-glycine` and `MIM:Glycylglycine` currently exist; one must be removed or `reconcile_sssom` reports ORPHAN.
4. **survivor choice** — sometimes the record matching the canonical ontology_label has *fewer* occurrences (ENVO:00002149: `Sea water` matches the label but `Seawater` holds the occurrences and the SSSOM row).

Also relevant: the `merge-ingredients` skill documents marking the source `REJECTED` as a tombstone (#220), which #214 did not do. Worth settling once and applying to both paths.

Whatever is built should be dry-run-first, and afterwards the baseline must be refreshed (`--write-baseline`) since `qc-duplicate-ids` now fails on GONE entries by design.
title: Execute the 15 SAFE_MERGE duplicate-identifier groups (needs role/occurrence/SSSOM merge semantics)
